reasoning_schema.system_prompt: You are a cognitive process analyst. You label the sentences of an AI model's reasoning trace. Always respond with valid JSON only: no prose, no explanation, no markdown code fences.

dimensions.name: framing
dimensions.definition: The sentence is about understanding the problem rather than solving it: restating or interpreting the request, listing or weighing the constraints, recalling what the task asks for, or deciding which approach, tool or strategy to use. A sentence that announces an intention ("I will start by...") is framing.

dimensions.name: solving
dimensions.definition: The sentence advances the answer itself: recalling a relevant fact, deducing, computing, drafting or revising candidate content, comparing options on their merits, or verifying a result already obtained. If the sentence contains a piece of the answer, or a step that produces one, it is solving.

dimensions.name: presentation
dimensions.definition: The sentence is about the form the final answer will take: format, length, structure, ordering, markdown, tone, register, or staying inside an assigned persona or role. Sentences about how something will be said, rather than what will be said, are presentation.

reasoning_schema.joint_template:
You are scoring the sentences of an AI model's reasoning trace along
{dimension_count} independent dimensions.

{dimension_definitions}

Rate every sentence from 0 to {intensity_scale} on EACH dimension:
  0 = the sentence has nothing to do with that dimension
  1 = the dimension is marginally present
  2 = the dimension is clearly present
  3 = the sentence is entirely about that dimension

The dimensions are independent, not a partition: a sentence may score high on more than
one, and a sentence that scores 0 everywhere is allowed. Read the whole trace for
context, but score each sentence on its own contribution.

[TASK THE MODEL WAS GIVEN]
{user_prompt}

[CRITERIA THE TASK WAS JUDGED AGAINST]
{criteria}

[REASONING TRACE, ONE NUMBERED SENTENCE PER LINE]
{numbered_units}

Respond with JSON shaped exactly like this, with one entry for every sentence id
listed above and no other keys:
{example_json}
reasoning_schema.metrics_template:
Analyze an AI model's reasoning trace together with the final response it produced.

[TASK THE MODEL WAS GIVEN]
{user_prompt}

[REASONING TRACE, ONE NUMBERED SENTENCE PER LINE]
{numbered_units}

[FINAL RESPONSE]
{candidate_response}

Report the following, citing sentence ids as evidence:
- alt_path_units: ids of the sentences where the model raises a DISTINCT alternative to a
  direction it is already pursuing or has just laid out - a different approach or strategy,
  or a different version of the answer itself. One id per distinct alternative, not one per
  later mention. Only count the later items if alternatives are presented as an up-front
  enumeration. Do not cite lists of requirements, sub-steps of a single plan, or pros and
  cons of one option.
- autocorrect_units: ids of the sentences where the model explicitly retracts or revises
  something it had just concluded ("wait", "actually", "that is wrong", "let me reconsider").
- alignment_score: 1-10, how faithfully the FINAL RESPONSE follows the conclusions the
  trace reached. 10 = the response implements them; 1 = the response ignores or
  contradicts them.
- alignment_evidence: if alignment_score is below 8, the ids of the sentences whose
  conclusions the response fails to honour. Empty list otherwise.

Respond with JSON and no other keys:
{{"alt_path_units": [], "autocorrect_units": [], "alignment_score": 0, "alignment_evidence": []}}

verdict_metadata.header:
# BENCHMARK METADATA
Each candidate saw only the PROMPT, the ATTACHMENT, and its own system prompt (not shown
here, and it may differ per candidate). The EVALUATION CRITERIA are the judges' rubric,
NOT shown to the candidate: missing one is a difference in behaviour, not disobedience.
verdict_metadata.figures:
Repetitions per candidate x test case: {repetitions}. Figures are mean +/- SD across them;
at 1 repetition every +/- is 0.00 by construction and says nothing about stability.
The OVERALL AGGREGATE tables carry means WITHOUT a deviation: pooled across test cases,
that spread is mostly the difference between tasks, not run-to-run stability. Read the
per-test-case sections when you need the +/-.
'Notes' come from the best-scoring repetition, not an average one.
Token counts are OUTPUT only: reasoning tokens are separate and excluded, input tokens
are not tracked.
verdict_metadata.score_scales:
Both scores run 1-10, but what they measure is set by this project's criteria and may be
redefined by the instructions below; 'N/A' means not computed.
verdict_metadata.cost_per_point:
'Think/point' is reasoning tokens divided by task score, so LOWER is cheaper. Treat it as
a diagnostic, never as a ranking: the task score floors at 1 rather than 0 and spans only
10x, while thinking tokens span far more, so a candidate that thinks little AND fails
scores well on it. Say what it shows, and rank on the scores themselves.
verdict_metadata.reasoning_profile:
Where a reasoning profile is shown, it describes the SHAPE of a thinking trace, not its
quality. Do not infer that a profile caused a score: candidates differ in more than one
respect at once, and the coverages are an LLM's reading of the trace. The aggregate
profile pools traces from tasks of different natures, so read it as a description of the
candidate's habits, not as a measurement of any one task. Report a profile as an
observation about behaviour, and say so when a claim about it is not supported by the
scores themselves. A trace marked as a provider summary is not the model's raw chain of
thought: its length, composition and self-correction counts reflect the summariser too,
so never rank a summarised trace against a raw one on those figures.
verdict_metadata.judge_llm: - llm-judge: graded 1-10 by an LLM against the test's criteria.
verdict_metadata.judge_similarity: - similarity: cosine similarity to a target text, rescaled to 1-10.
verdict_metadata.judge_assert:
- assert: a user-authored Python expression; it may use the full 1-10 range or just a
  pass/fail pair, and which one is never declared.
verdict_metadata.judge_types_mixed:
These are DIFFERENT judges, so their scores are not comparable across test cases, and the
aggregate above pools all of them: read it as an indication, not a measurement.
verdict_metadata.global_criteria_intro: How the global score was produced:
verdict_metadata.global_criteria_llm:
- llm-judge: graded 1-10 by an LLM against these criteria:
  {criteria_text}
verdict_metadata.global_criteria_similarity:
- similarity: cosine similarity (scale 1-10) to this target response:
  {criteria_text}
verdict_metadata.global_criteria_assert:
- assert: a user-authored Python expression evaluated against the response:
  {criteria_text}
verdict_metadata.global_criteria_none: Global scoring is disabled for this project.
